snake-antivenom-indication.l: Spontaneous bleeding away from the bite
Neurotoxic signs (drooping eyelids, eye movement paralysis, weakness)
Low blood pressure, shock, abnormal rhythm or ECG
Swelling of more than half the bitten limb (within 48 hours, no tourniquet)
Bite on a finger or toe, with swelling
Rapidly spreading swelling (past the wrist or ankle within hours)
Enlarged tender lymph node draining the limb (Asia)
Africa: species known to cause tissue death (Bitis, Echis, Cerastes, Macrovipera, spitting cobras)
Previous reaction to horse or sheep serum, or severe allergy or asthma

Asia: bitten in Maluku or West Papua (Indonesia)
